messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: HIGH - gpu-prefill-oom on prod-serving (cluster-prod-3) at 2026-02-18T14:17:56Z
pagerduty-bot: Paging Chris (oncall) :rotating_light: (priority: P1)
Chris (oncall): acked, jumping in. Any customer impact?
Leo (customer-success): seeing errors from 2 customers - requests returning 500s from the hosted API; one reported timeouts in their game ingestion flow.
Sara (runtime): quick summary — container repeatedly OOMs during prefill phase when processing large context/prompt. Kube shows CrashLoopBackOff for pod runtime-ml-64-pool-7.
Anya (sre): linking recent node events: node prod-gpu-07 has GPU driver resets ~14:15-14:18 and kubelet restarted container twice. Could be memory spike plus driver OOM.
Mike (eng-runtime): logs from the failing container (tail):
```
I05018 14:16:58.123 PrefillManager: received request id=abc123, prefill_tokens=112k, model=gptx-64k
E05018 14:17:01.321 Runtime: CUDA out of memory while allocating 12.8 GiB
W05018 14:17:01.322 ContainerRuntime: restarting container (exit code 137)
```
Chris (oncall): 112k prefill? that's huge. Is this customer using a streaming prefill or full prefill packaged?
Sara (runtime): looks like a non-streaming prefill (we allocate full KV cache up front for gptx-64k). KV/cache size scales with context length; 112k blows past our per-pod assumed max. We don't yet have server-side prefill limits for this model.
Chris (oncall): immediate mitigations we can do now?
Anya (sre): isolate node: cordon prod-gpu-07 to avoid further noisy restarts while we triage.
Mike (eng-runtime): pushing hotfix: deny prefill requests > 64k tokens with a 429 response from the proxy (config change). Will roll out canary to one region. Command: `kubectl apply -f runtime-configmap-hotfix.yaml`
deploy-bot: Starting rollout of configmap runtime-configmap-hotfix to deployment runtime-proxy-prod-canary...
Chris (oncall): Sara, can we gracefully reject without crashing the runtime? Need to ensure 429s surface to customers not 500s.
Sara (runtime): yes - proxy will short-circuit and return 429 before creating containers. Runtime change too risky to deploy cluster-wide immediately. Canarying.
Leo (customer-success): notifying the two affected customers that we're rolling a mitigation, ETA ~10m; will offer temporary quota increases or suggest chunking their prefill.
Mike (eng-runtime): canary applied to us-west-2 small subset. Monitoring logs now.
```
# on the canary pod logs
I05018 14:20:05.987 Proxy: request id=abc123 prefill_tokens=112k -> rejected (prefill_limit=64k)
I05018 14:20:06.004 Proxy: returned 429 to client
```
Anya (sre): node cordoned. No new pods scheduled on prod-gpu-07. Existing noisy pods terminated.
Chris (oncall): any memory pressure on other nodes?
Sara (runtime): other nodes show increased memory utilization but below eviction thresholds. We're adding an alert to detect prefill-token spikes >50k to page oncall next time.
Mike (eng-runtime): also opened short-term fallback: route requests that declare >32k tokens to gptx-32k (smaller context variant) with a notice to client. Implemented via routing policy change.
deploy-bot: Routing policy update deployed to runtime-router-prod in 2 regions.
Leo (customer-success): both customers confirmed they got 429 now instead of 500s, and one switched to chunked prefill per our suggestion; errors reduced.
Chris (oncall): good. Any remaining crashes?
Sara (runtime): no new CrashLoopBackOffs in the last 8 minutes. Crash rate down to baseline.
Anya (sre): schedule follow-up: postmortem + action items. Suggest: add hard prefill token limit at proxy, better client-facing error with guidance, telemetry to log declared prefill token sizes, and a quota/guardrail for heavy users.
Mike (eng-runtime): action items I'm taking: 1) make proxy prefill limit permanent with config flag and rollout by EOD, 2) add prefill token histogram to runtime metrics, 3) add graceful spill-to-streaming prefill for large contexts (design PR).
Leo (customer-success): I'll coordinate comms and check for any additional impacted customers in the last 24h.
Chris (oncall): thanks team. I'm closing the active paging once we confirm 30m stable. Leaving notes in PD.
incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated (container restarts halted), severity downgraded to SEV2.
Sara (runtime): postmortem draft will include exact memory numbers per token for gptx-64k and recommended default prefill limit of 64k tokens.
Anya (sre): follow-up checklist: update runbooks, add alert for driver resets + OOM combination, and ensure we cordon nodes automatically on noisy GPU driver resets.
Mike (eng-runtime): sample quick command we used: `kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=runtime -o wide` and `kubectl logs runtime-ml-64-pool-7 -c runtime | grep \"CUDA out of memory\" -n`
Chris (oncall): thanks all. I'll hand off to Mike for the hotfix rollout notes and to Leo for customer comms.
Mike (eng-runtime): note for postmortem — the request was legitimate workload from a game replay system; we should work on best-practice docs for large-context ingestion.
Leo (customer-success): customers appreciated the proactive 429; minor frustration but no data loss. Will include suggested client changes in follow-up.
Chris (oncall): closing thread in 30m if stable. :white_check_mark:
